newsitem.title: USA: Southwest Air sees Q3 EPS ahead of year ago.
newsitem.headline: Southwest Air sees Q3 EPS ahead of year ago.

text.p: Southwest Airlines Inc's chief financial officer on Thursday said he expected the carrier's third-quarter earnings to exceed the $0.40-a-share profit reported for the same period a year ago.

Gary Kelly would not comment on how Southwest would perform against Wall Street analysts' estimates for the current third quarter. "But we would expect to beat last year's third-quarter earnings," he said.
The latest First Call consensus earnings per share estimate for the third quarter is $0.53 per share.
While the outlook for the airline is strong, Kelly said it would be "difficult" for the airline to match the second-quarter results posted earlier Thursday.
"The second quarter is typically our strongest," he told reporters during a conference call.

Southwest beat Wall Street estimates by $0.03 per share with second-quarter earnings of $0.62 a share, or $93.8 million, on revenues of $956.9 million. In the 1996 quarter, the company earned $0.56 per share, or $85.3 million, on revenues of $910.3 million.
Kelly said the positive outlook for the current quarter reflected low fuel prices and the strong revenue momentum coming out of the second quarter.

Second-quarter fuel prices were just 1.7 percent higher than in the same period last year, while revenues improved by 5.1 percent. For the first six months of 1997, revenues rose 9.6 percent year over year.
Kelly said he expected no significant rise in fuel prices in the near term while the revenue outlook remains strong "for the quarter or so at least."
"The airline industry on the whole is doing quite well, and we have a stable route system and our bookings in place remain solid," he said.
